metadata.expected_behavior: skill identifies missing critical fields and requests them before proceeding with case classification

turns.speaker: Bernadette Olufemi
turns.text: Thanks for holding, Mr. Halverson-Brace. I've got your file pulled up — looks like you spoke with our front desk yesterday and they scheduled this callback. I just want to walk through the basics of what happened so we can decide together whether this is something our firm can help with. Sound okay?

turns.speaker: Quentin Halverson-Brace
turns.text: Yeah, that's fine. I'll tell you up front I've never done anything like this before so I might be a little scattered. My wife is the one who pushed me to call. She thinks I'm being too easygoing about it.

turns.speaker: Bernadette Olufemi
turns.text: That's completely fine. Let's start at the top — can you tell me, in your own words, what happened?

turns.speaker: Quentin Halverson-Brace
turns.text: Sure. So it was April 27th, a Sunday afternoon. I was at the indoor climbing gym I've been a member at for about three years — Skyhook Vertical, the one on Roosevelt near downtown. I'd just finished a route on the lead wall and was walking back toward the bouldering area. The floor in the transition hallway between the two rooms had been mopped, I guess, but there was no sign out, no cone, nothing. I was wearing climbing shoes which have basically zero traction on a wet polished floor. I went down hard. Right hip, right elbow, and the back of my head clipped the wall on the way down. There were maybe six or seven people in that area who saw it happen. The shift manager came over within probably a minute. His name was on a tag — I want to say Travis or Trevor — and he was apologetic and made me sign an incident report. They offered to comp my next month, which felt insulting honestly. My wife drove me to Mercy Gilbert that night because I was lightheaded and couldn't put weight on the right leg without it buckling.

turns.speaker: Bernadette Olufemi
turns.text: Okay, that's a really clear picture, thank you. A couple of clarifying questions. When you say you went to Mercy Gilbert — what did they tell you there? Any fractures, any imaging done?

turns.speaker: Quentin Halverson-Brace
turns.text: They did a CT for the head and X-rays of the hip and elbow. I want to say everything 'came back clean' is the phrase they used. So no broken bones according to them. They diagnosed me with — I'm going to butcher this — some kind of soft tissue thing. A contusion, I think they said. And they were watching the head injury but I didn't have any of the bad concussion signs so they sent me home with a sheet about what to watch for. I followed up with my primary, Dr. Sundara at Coronado Family Medicine, the following Tuesday. She referred me to an orthopedist because the hip was still really bad. I saw the orthopedist last Thursday, May 8th. He took new films and ordered an MRI which I have scheduled for the 22nd. He gave me a name for what's going on but I genuinely cannot remember what he said. It's something with letters, like an acronym. I'm sorry. My wife wrote it down somewhere. The upshot is I'm walking with a cane right now, I can't sleep on my right side, I haven't been back to the gym obviously, and he's telling me to expect this to be a multi-month thing. I've also got tingling down my right arm from the elbow that's new this week, which is freaking me out a little.

turns.speaker: Bernadette Olufemi
turns.text: I appreciate that — and please don't apologize, this is exactly the kind of thing we follow up on. Let me ask about the gym itself. Skyhook Vertical — is that a single location, locally owned, or part of a chain? Do you know who actually owns or operates the facility?

turns.speaker: Quentin Halverson-Brace
turns.text: That is a great question and I don't have a good answer for you. When I signed up three years ago I'm pretty sure I signed a membership agreement and a waiver — everyone does, it's standard for climbing gyms. I think the LLC name on the paperwork was different from 'Skyhook Vertical' because that's just the brand. Something with a number in it? Like 'Roosevelt 12 Holdings' or 'Apex something LLC,' I really can't remember. I think there's a second Skyhook location in Tempe but I don't know if it's the same owners or franchised. The shift manager that day, Travis or Trevor, I don't have a last name for him. I never got the owner's name. I haven't been back to ask — I didn't want to seem like I was building a case before I even talked to a lawyer. I do still have the membership app on my phone if that helps.

turns.speaker: Bernadette Olufemi
turns.text: It helps a lot. The membership agreement and any waiver language are going to matter, so hold onto everything in the app. Now — and I'll come back to this if it's a hard question — can you describe the actual injury as your orthopedist explained it? You mentioned an acronym, the cane, the tingling. Has he given you a working diagnosis or a treatment plan in writing?

turns.speaker: Quentin Halverson-Brace
turns.text: Honestly, no, not in writing that I've gotten yet. The visit summary in his portal just lists CPT codes and the impression line is two or three abbreviated words I can't make sense of. He talked about it being a labrum issue but then also said the MRI would tell him if it was that or something else, so I think he was guessing. He also mentioned the elbow tingling could be a nerve thing — ulnar maybe? — and said if it's still happening at the MRI we'd image that too. I want to give you a clean answer like 'I have a torn labrum and ulnar neuropathy' but I'd be making that up. The real story is I'm in pain, I'm using a cane, the MRI is in a week, and I don't have a confirmed diagnosis yet. I can pull up the visit summary from my phone and forward it to you after we get off the call.

turns.speaker: Bernadette Olufemi
turns.text: That would be very helpful. Please forward the Mercy Gilbert discharge paperwork, the primary care visit notes, the orthopedist's visit summary, the MRI order, and the incident report from Skyhook if you have a copy. And take photos of any bruising you still have. We'll start there. I want to be straight with you: there are two pieces I need before I can route this to an attorney for review. The first is who, legally, owns the premises — the operating entity behind Skyhook Vertical. The second is a clearer medical picture, which we'll have after the MRI and the follow-up. Once those come in we can talk again. Does that work?

turns.speaker: Quentin Halverson-Brace
turns.text: That works. I'll get the membership paperwork to you today and the medical stuff as it comes in. I really appreciate you walking me through this. My wife is going to be relieved I finally called.

intake_specialist_notes: Client gave a detailed account but could not identify the legal owner/operator of the premises — only the brand name 'Skyhook Vertical' and possible LLC fragments. This needs to be established before attorney review.

Injury picture is unresolved: no fracture per ER, working diagnoses from orthopedist unconfirmed, MRI scheduled 2026-05-22. New neurological symptom (right-arm tingling) reported one week prior to call. Cannot classify severity until MRI results and follow-up exam are documented.
Client tone cooperative and forthcoming; not refusing disclosure — genuinely does not have the information.
